title: Knightmare.
transcript: Knight to c7 check forces the king to move away from the corner, but now there is an issue. The white pawn is only one step away from getting a new queen. So, black has to be very careful and continue with knight to a6 check. Now, the king has two options, either to go to the corner or to come outside. Of course, going to the corner would not be a good idea because after knight to b6, this would be a double knight checkmate. So, the king has to try coming out in the open. And now it seems like white [music] is kind of out of the woods. He's going to promote on the next move and it is going to be very hard to stop that. And this time, this move is not a checkmate. The king can simply move away. So, has black failed in trying to attack this white king? Well, not exactly. Black continues with king to e8, now setting up the same checkmate threat. You cannot now get a queen because this would be a double knight checkmate. And for a moment it seems like the dark knight is going to get his revenge on the white knight from the previous game. But then he gets the cold shower. White promotes to another [music] knight and we are again in a position where both players have two knights each and it seems like white has successfully stopped the checkmate threat. But unfortunately, black is not done. And surprisingly, after king to e7, white is in zugzwang. There are no moves that don't lose the game. Moving this knight would simply allow this checkmate. And moving the other knight would allow this checkmate. And black wins this incredible game.
